title: The Table From Heaven: A Dialogue on Doubt
script: Host: [warmly] Tonight's discussion centers on a request the disciples of Isa made, asking for a table spread from heaven. Pak Hasan, thank you for joining us.
Pak Hasan: [pleasant] My pleasure. It's a compact story, but it carries an unusual amount of psychological nuance for its length.
Host: [curious] Remind our listeners how the request itself is phrased. It's not simply a demand for food, is it?
Pak Hasan: [thoughtful] Not at all. They frame it as wanting to eat from it, to have their hearts reassured, and to know with certainty that Isa had spoken truthfully to them.
Host: [interested] That's a striking admission, isn't it, coming from people who had already witnessed him perform other miracles beforehand.
Pak Hasan: [nodding] Exactly, which is what makes the moment so honest rather than embarrassing. Belief, even among close companions, apparently still craved reinforcement occasionally.
Host: [curious] How does Isa initially respond to the request?

Pak Hasan: [reflective] With visible caution, actually. He urges them to remain conscious of Allah if they're genuinely believers, almost testing whether the request stems from faith or simple appetite.
Host: [thoughtful] So he isn't eager to grant it immediately.
Pak Hasan: [agreeing] Right, and I think that hesitation is deliberate. Miracles aren't vending machines; each one carries consequence for those who witness it and then fail to honor it afterward.
Host: [curious] And yet he does eventually pray for it.
Pak Hasan: [warm] He does, asking that it become a recurring festival, a sign from Allah, and sustenance, appealing directly for provision on their behalf as their best provider.
Host: [interested] What happens once the table actually descends?
Pak Hasan: [firm] That's the part rarely emphasized enough. Allah warns immediately afterward that whoever disbelieves following this will face a punishment unlike any given to others in creation.
Host: [reflective] So the miracle raises the stakes rather than simply settling the matter comfortably.
Pak Hasan: [thoughtful] Precisely, which I think is the real lesson buried here, that certainty, once granted so vividly, becomes accountability, not mere comfort.
Host: [warm] A generous request, then, with a rather sobering condition quietly attached to it.
Pak Hasan: [warm] Exactly that tension, and I suspect it's why the story still unsettles people who read it closely instead of skimming past it.

quiz.question: How did the disciples phrase their request for the table?
options: Simply as a demand for food
As wanting reassured hearts and certainty that Isa had spoken truthfully
As a test of Isa's power alone
As a request for wealth
quiz.explanation: They framed it as wanting to eat from it, have their hearts reassured, and know with certainty that Isa had spoken truthfully.

quiz.question: How does Pak Hasan interpret the disciples already having seen other miracles?
options: It proves the request was insincere
It shows belief, even among close companions, still craved occasional reinforcement
It means the request was unnecessary
It contradicts the rest of the story
quiz.explanation: Pak Hasan says this makes the moment honest rather than embarrassing, since belief still craved reinforcement occasionally.

quiz.question: How does Isa initially respond to the request?
options: He grants it immediately without hesitation
He urges them to remain conscious of Allah first, testing their motive
He refuses outright
He ignores the request
quiz.explanation: He responds with visible caution, urging them to remain conscious of Allah if they're genuinely believers.

quiz.question: What does Isa ask for when he does pray for the table?
options: Only food for himself
That it become a recurring festival, a sign, and sustenance
Wealth for the disciples
A private miracle no one else could see
quiz.explanation: He asks that it become a recurring festival, a sign from Allah, and sustenance, provided directly for them.

quiz.question: What warning follows the descent of the table?
options: No warning is given
Whoever disbelieves afterward will face an unmatched punishment
The disciples must fast for a year
The table would never appear again
quiz.explanation: Allah warns that whoever disbelieves following this will face a punishment unlike any given to others in creation.
